prompt.context: Your client is an Italian television broadcasting company. It has acquired the rights to broadcast the Champions League Soccer Tournament in Italy. You have been asked to decide whether to broadcast it on the pay-TV channel owned by the client or on the free (ad-supported) channel also owned by the client.
prompt.question: What should the client do — broadcast Champions League games on its pay-TV channel or its free TV channel?

clarifying_info.q: What are the revenue sources for each option?
clarifying_info.a: Free TV earns advertising revenue; pay-TV earns incremental subscribers.
30 seconds of ads cost $70K at any stage of the tournament. Games have 25 minutes of advertising.

First round: 4 groups of 4 teams each; each team plays every other team in its group (round-robin, neutral field); top 2 teams per group advance. Second round: quarterfinals with home and away games. Third round: semifinals (home and away). Then the final game.

clarifying_info.q: How many Italian teams are there, and which games does the client broadcast?
clarifying_info.a: There are 3 Italian teams, each in a different group. The client broadcasts only games involving at least one Italian team. Assume all Italian teams advance through all rounds.

clarifying_info.q: What is the opportunity cost if we choose free TV?
clarifying_info.a: If a game is not broadcast on free TV, the client still earns $20K per minute of advertising from alternative programming in that slot.

clarifying_info.q: What is the incremental subscriber uplift for pay-TV?
clarifying_info.a: Broadcasting on pay-TV would bring 1 million additional subscribers for the year.

clarifying_info.q: What are the pay-TV subscription economics?
clarifying_info.a: Subscription fee (sign-up) is $10; monthly price is $5. Customer acquisition cost is $5 per new subscriber; annual cost to serve one account is $6. No existing customers leave if the client does not broadcast on pay-TV. The project lasts only 1 year.

framework: Define the decision: compare incremental profit of free TV vs. pay-TV broadcast option
Calculate the number of games to broadcast (tournament structure x Italian teams)
Free TV: compute incremental ad revenue per game vs. opportunity cost alternative
Pay TV: compute incremental subscriber revenue minus acquisition and service costs
Compare net incremental profit of both scenarios and recommend the higher-value option
Identify qualitative factors and risks that could shift the recommendation

questions.prompt: How many games does the client broadcast in total?
questions.guidance: Walk through each round systematically. Round 1: 3 Italian teams, each in a group of 4 — each plays 3 round-robin games, so 3 × 3 = 9 games. Round 2 (quarterfinals): 3 Italian teams advancing means 3 two-legged ties = 6 games. Round 3 (semifinals): 3 Italian teams advancing — but only 4 teams remain, so at most 2 ties = 4 games (assume all 3 advance as instructed). Final: 1 game. Total: 9 + 6 + 4 + 1 = 20 games.

math.setup: Count games per round for Italian-involved matches
steps: Round 1: 3 Italian teams × 3 group-stage games each = 9 games
Round 2 (QF, home+away): 3 Italian teams × 2 legs = 6 games
Round 3 (SF, home+away): assumption all advance → 4 SF games (2 ties × 2 legs)

questions.prompt: What is the incremental revenue per game on free TV, accounting for opportunity cost?
questions.guidance: Revenue per game = 25 min × 2 slots/min × $70K = $3.5M. But without broadcasting the Champion's League game, the slot earns $20K/min. So the incremental revenue is 25 min × ($140K – $20K) = 25 × $120K = $3M per game. (Alternatively: $3.5M – $0.5M opportunity cost = $3M.)

math.setup: Ad revenue per game minus opportunity cost of alternative programming

questions.prompt: What is the total incremental profit for the free TV scenario?
questions.guidance: Multiply incremental revenue per game by total games. No additional costs on the free TV side.

math.setup: Total incremental profit = incremental revenue per game × number of games

questions.prompt: What is the total incremental profit for the pay-TV scenario?
questions.guidance: Revenue from 1M new subscribers: each pays $10 sign-up fee + $5/month × 12 months = $70 total per subscriber → 1M × $70 = $70M. Costs: acquisition ($5/subscriber) + annual service ($6/subscriber) = $11/subscriber → 1M × $11 = $11M. Net profit = $70M – $11M = $59M.

math.setup: Incremental revenue minus acquisition and service costs for 1M new subscribers

brainstorming.prompt: Are there any other factors or strategic considerations that could affect the recommendation beyond the 1-year financial calculation?

categories.name: Pay-TV upside / optionality
ideas: New pay-TV subscribers may renew in subsequent years, generating recurring revenue beyond year 1
Cross-selling opportunities to new subscribers (other sports packages, on-demand content)
Higher subscriber base strengthens negotiating power with content providers
Pay-TV subscribers tend to be higher-value, more engaged customers

categories.name: Free TV strategic benefits
ideas: Broader audience reach strengthens advertising rates for future programming
Brand building and market presence in soccer broadcasting
Opportunity to attract new advertisers seeking large audiences
Potential to upsell free TV viewers to pay-TV channel over time

categories.name: Assumption sensitivity
ideas: If Italian teams are eliminated early, the number of games and total revenue fall sharply — especially impactful for free TV
Pay-TV subscriber estimate of 1M may be uncertain; a lower figure would reduce pay-TV attractiveness
Ad rates could vary by round (e.g., finals may command premium prices)
Churn of new pay-TV subscribers after the tournament ends reduces LTV

categories.name: Regulatory / rights considerations
ideas: Rights agreement may mandate free-to-air broadcast for certain high-profile matches
Regulatory requirements around public access to major sporting events in Italy

recommendation: Broadcast Champions League games on the free TV channel
Free TV generates $60M incremental profit vs. $59M for pay-TV — a $1M advantage — with no incremental cost risk
The free TV option avoids the execution risk embedded in the pay-TV subscriber acquisition assumption
risks: Italian teams eliminated early would significantly reduce the number of games and free TV ad revenue
The 1M subscriber uplift assumption for pay-TV may be understated; if actual uplift is higher, pay-TV could be more profitable
Ad rate assumption ($70K/30s) held constant across all rounds; finals likely command higher rates
next_steps: Validate the 1M subscriber assumption with market research and historical data from comparable sports broadcasts
Model scenarios where Italian teams exit at different rounds to stress-test the free TV revenue figure
Explore whether year-2+ subscriber retention on pay-TV materially changes the NPV comparison
Assess any regulatory obligations regarding free-to-air access to Champions League games in Italy
